title: Person
description:
A Person is an individual template — the kind of human the organization deals with. Examples: Employee, Customer, Patient, Borrower, Contractor, Partner, Associate. A Person is a type, not a specific named individual; instance-level data (Joe, Jane, Dr. Adams) lives in Product/Technical layers.

Person is one of four noun primitives (alongside Resource, Position, Group). All four share the noun base shape: name, optional attributes[], optional actions[], optional parent. Person carries no people-specific fields beyond the shared base — its identity as a Person comes from being declared in the Domain's persons[] collection.

name.description: The singular PascalCase name of the Person template.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of who this Person template represents.

domain.description: The home Domain this Person belongs to, referenced by Domain `name` (the authored form of the primary `belongs_to` edge). Names a Domain in the document's `domain` root or flat `domains[]`.

attributes.description: Fields that describe this Person template.

actions.description: Verbs this Person template supports — the catalog of lifecycle actions on the Person itself (Patient.GetAdmitted, Customer.Onboard, Employee.Hire). Distinct from actions a Person performs in a Position context (those are Operations targeted at other nouns, assigned via Tasks).

parent.description: Optional parent Person name (e.g., for specialization hierarchies).

resource.description: Optional Resource template that backs this Person — used when a Person template is a façade over a Resource at another layer (e.g., Customer Person backed by Customer Resource).

examples.description: Representative example records for this Person template.

examples.name: Patient
examples.description: A person receiving care from the organization.

examples.name: Borrower
examples.description: A person applying for or holding a loan.
